message.content:
A common mistake people make with "it" is using it incorrectly as a pronoun when the antecedent (the noun it refers to) is unclear or ambiguous. For example:

❌ *"When the dog chased the cat, it ran fast."*

This sentence is ambiguous—did the dog or the cat run fast? The pronoun "it" doesn't clearly refer to either, leading to confusion.

✅ Better: *"When the dog chased the cat, the cat ran fast."* or *"When the dog chased the cat, the dog ran fast."*

To avoid this mistake, always ensure that "it" clearly refers to a specific, previously mentioned noun. Clarity and precision in pronoun usage help make writing more effective and easier to understand.
